title: OpenBSP message content, version 1
description: The `content` column of public.messages for rows with version "1". Generated from supabase/functions/_shared/types/message_types.ts; do not edit by hand.

MessageContentV1.description: `messages.content` for version "1": what any direction can store.

file.description: Construct a type with the properties of T except for those in type K.

data.description: Construct a type with a set of properties K of type T

name.description: Service-native emoji id, e.g. Slack "thumbsup", Discord custom-emoji id; for Meta the Unicode emoji itself.

unicode.description: Unicode rendering, e.g. "👍" — absent only for emoji with no Unicode form (custom workspace emoji) and Meta removals.

IncomingMessage.description:
WhatsApp Messages Text (caption for media types) Media (File) Data

Text and/or Media (up to two parts), or Data (one part)

Excepting Reaction, Contacts and Location, all other types differ depending on the direction (incoming or outgoing)

FilePart.description: Represents a file, such as an image, video, or document. WhatsApp allows media messages to include an accompanying text caption. For now, this caption is embedded directly within the `text` attribute of the `FilePart`. A more structured approach, leveraging the `Parts` type, would involve separate `FilePart` and `TextPart` components for such messages in the future.

category.description: H3: the closed category of an escalation, when the note records one.

AssignmentData.description: H1 — the audit note of an assignment, written by public.set_conversation_assignment: who was answering, who is now, who decided and why. Record-only (it always carries `internal`), never dispatched, and never part of the history the model reads.

Mention.description: A mention — who the text calls out. Dual-keyed the way authorship is: `address` in contact space (a WhatsApp participant's digits, a Slack user id), `agent_id` in member space; either or both may be set. `name` is the display text as it appears in `text` ("@Ana" ⇒ name "Ana"), which is also how dispatchers find the token to re-encode natively (Slack `<@U…>`, WhatsApp `@digits` + MentionedJID). Soft references like `re_message_id`: tolerant of absence, never a FK.

name.description: Service-native emoji id, e.g. Slack "thumbsup", Discord custom-emoji id; for Meta the Unicode emoji itself.

unicode.description: Unicode rendering, e.g. "👍" — absent only for emoji with no Unicode form (custom workspace emoji) and Meta removals.

internal.description: Record-only: this row is never dispatched, to anyone. Declared here so the marker travels with the content instead of living in a column readers must know to consult. Writers set it themselves AND insert the row unarmed (status {}, no pending) — agent-client does both on tool traces and errors; the database reads the marker (dispatch and agent triggers refuse it) but never stamps or strips anything.
